decision_maker: Director of Housing and Communities - Vicky McDermott
purpose:
The Domestic Abuse Act 2021 placed a new
statutory duty on local authorities to ensure that victims and
survivors of domestic abuse and their children can access the right
support, within refuges and other types of domestic abuse safe
accommodation, when they need it.
Since November 2023, Newcastle City Council has commissioned and
procured services from the provider ‘Changing Lives’ to
deliver the Newcastle Integrated Domestic Abuse Service (NIDAS).
The provision of these services supports the Council to meet our
domestic abuse statutory duty by keeping people safe in our purpose
built refuge and safe living in their own homes in the community
with dedicated support and through recognising children as victims
in their own right. In the government’s new VAWG Strategy
(2025), they have emphasised the importance of early intervention
with children to protect them from future violence and of changing
the attitudes and beliefs that lead to VAWG. The commissioning
arrangements for the ‘NIDAS’ service were put in place
following an open tender exercise and are in place until November
2027.
The ‘NIDAS’ service provides a coordinated,
whole-system response to domestic abuse as the city’s core
offer. The service is designed to deliver integrated support across
adults, children and families, recognising children as victims in
their own right. The intention of this integrated model was to
enable
the identification of gaps in provision and emerging need across
the system; this has highlighted increasing demand for dedicated
support for children and young people, which current capacity is
insufficient to meet.
We are requesting approval to Directly Award contracts to the
providers ‘Action for Children’ and ‘Children
North East’.
content:
The delegated officer, Director of Housing and
Communities is recommended to:
• Authorise the Direct Awarding
of contracts, to the providers ‘Action for Children’
and ‘Children North East’;
• Authorise the Assistant
Director for Law and Governance, to complete the necessary
documentation.

content:
Planning permission for application reference 2026/0419/01/DET
be refused for the following reasons:
 
 
i. 
The proposed development, by reason of its design,
fails to positively respond to built
landscapes, does not take a comprehensive and coordinated approach
to development, has failed to use material, colours and tones
appropriate to the characteristics of the area contrary to the
requirements of the National Planning Policy Framework, Policy CS15
of the Core Strategy and Urban Core Plan and Policy DM20 of the
Development and Allocations Plan.
 
 
ii. 
The development would increase in car trips and does
not promote or enhance public transport; has failed to adequately
mitigate against its impact on the highway network in the interest
of safety, efficiency and accessibility; and failed to demonstrate
that the residual cumulative impacts would not be severe and the
development has failed to demonstrate highway network capacity and
operation, contrary to the requirements of National Planning Policy
Framework, Policy CS13 of the Core Strategy and Urban Core Plan and
Policies DM10, DM12 & DM14 of the Development and Allocations
Plan.
 
 
iii. 
The development has failed to assess and mitigate
air quality to demonstrate that there is no unacceptable adverse
environmental and health impact, contrary to the requirements of
National Planning Policy Framework, Policy CS14 of the Core
Strategy and Urban Core Plan and Policy DM24 of the Development and
Allocations Plan.
 
 
iv. 
The development has failed to prioritise the use of
SuDS, failing to separate, minimise and control surface water
runoff, has failed to manage and reduce flood risk, by failing to
maximise permeable surfaces and incorporate green infrastructure,
failing to demonstrate that its surface water drainage strategy,
site layout and design will not increase the risk of flooding
elsewhere and that exceedance flows will be managed, failed to
manage surface water as close to source as possible using source
control measures, failed to follow the SuDS management train
approach to manage water quantity and quality throughout the site,
failed to provide the most sustainable SuDS techniques from the
SuDS Hierarchy, failed to demonstrate the life-time maintenance and
management of the SuDS, contrary to the requirements of the
National Planning Policy Framework, Policy CS16 of the Core
Strategy and Urban Core Plan and Policy DM26 of the Development and
Allocations Plan.

decision_maker: Director of Housing and Communities - Vicky McDermott
purpose:
This report proposes
the extension of the current Public Spaces Protection Order (PSPO)
for Newcastle City-wide. Newcastle City Council continues to face
problems with anti-social behaviour. People who live and work in
the city have raised concerns, and the Council wants to make sure
Newcastle stays a safe and welcoming place. To help with this, the
Council wants to extend the PSPO currently in place to continue to
utilise the enforcement powers to reduce anti-social behaviour and
to make sure support is available for people who need it.

If the extension is approved, it will include two current
behaviours: Drinking in public spaces and the Dog
Control/fouling.

Public Space Protection Orders (‘PSPOs’) were created
by the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014, Chapter
2, Part 4 which came into force on 20 October 2014. PSPO’s
can be used to regulate activities in public places that can have a
negative effect on the quality of life of those in the locality.
They are designed to ensure that the law-abiding majority can use
and enjoy public spaces, safe from anti-social behaviour. Further
information can be found on the following links.
 
The current PSPO is
due to expire on 19 June 2026. While there has been local agreement
to undertake consultation and bring forward proposals for a new
PSPO – potentially encompassing a broader range of behaviours
– at a future Cabinet meeting, to avoid any gap in provision
we are seeking an extension of the current order and will consult
separately for an additional PSPO to go to Cabinet at a later
date.

due to expire on 19 June 2026 but the behaviours being controlled

support of retaining the existing measures. The extension will
continue the existing conditions, including:

causing antisocial behaviour because of alcohol. These rules are
not meant to stop normal, peaceful activities. For example,
families having a picnic in the park or people enjoying a drink in
their own garden.

The PSPO is meant to have one set of rules for the whole area. The
aim is to stop alcohol related behaviour that is upsetting or
harmful to local communities.

Those that are causing issues, a person shall stop consuming
alcohol or surrender any containers (sealed or unsealed) which are
reasonably believed to contain alcohol, when required to do so by
an Authorised officer.

on leads and dog fouling. The proposed extension of the PSPO would

making by 30th June 2026 and to carry out early scoping
consultation in July 2026
content:

sought to issue a notice of intention to to commence local plan
making by 30th June 2026 and to carry out early scoping
consultation in July 2026

Cabinet agreed to:
 

i) 
Approve the issuing and publication of notices of intention in
Appendix 1 by 30 June 2026, and to pass through “Gateway
1” by 31 October 2026 which commences the 30 month Local Plan
preparation process.

 

ii) 
Approve publication of the Local Plan timetables.
 

iii) 
Grant delegated authority to the Assistant Director of Planning and
the Portfolio Holder to take all necessary steps to progress the
preparation of the Local Plan through the three statutory Gateways
as detailed in Appendix 2 of the report.
 

iv) 
Approve the governance arrangements set out in Appendix 3 of the
report, including setting up a Joint Members Steering Group and
Joint Cross Party Member Panel to provide political oversight of
preparation of the Local Plan.
 

v) 
Approve the carrying out of early scoping consultation in relation
to the Communications and Engagement Strategy in Appendix 4 and the
Scope of the Local Plan in Appendix 5 of the report.
 

vi) 
Approve the progression and preparation of an evidence base for the
Local Plan and delegate authority the Assistant Director of
Planning in consultation with the Portfolio Holder to publish
evidence studies/assessments.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to commence the local plan making process and carry out early scoping consultation.

content:
This report will seek
approval for Newcastle's Best Start in Life Plan for 2026-2029,
which will set out areas of priority focus and action to deliver
the national targets for improved Good Level of Development of
Newcastle children at the end of their school reception year.

Cabinet agreed to:
 

i) 
Approve the Newcastle Best Start in Life Plan 2026-2029

 

ii) 
Note the use of the Best Start Family Hubs and Healthy Babies grant
and associated external funding streams to help us deliver on this
Plan by building workforce capacity, strengthening evidence-based
interventions and enabling consistent delivery of the expanded Best
Start offer.

oversight from the Newcastle Children and Young People’s
Strategic Partnership and operational direction from the Best Start
Steering Group, to ensure coordinated delivery across
Children’s Services, Health, Early Years, Public Health and
wider partners.

purpose:

Cabinet approval for the Council to take part in the expansion of
the Regional Fostering Hub in line with the Department for
Education (DfE) expansion programme. The project seeks to improve
the experiences of foster carers and enable a more consistent high
quality support offer for applicants and existing foster carers,
resulting in increased sufficiency of family
based care for children in our care.
content:
This report will seek
Cabinet approval for the Council to take part in the expansion of
the Regional Fostering Hub in line with the Department for
Education (DfE) expansion programme. The project seeks to improve
the experiences of foster carers and enable a more consistent high
quality support offer for applicants and existing foster carers,
resulting in increased sufficiency of family
based care for children in our care.
 

Cabinet agreed to:
 

i) 
Give final approval for Newcastle City Council to enter into an
agreement to be part of the expanded North East Fostering Hub in
line with national policy and guidance.

 

ii) 
Endorse agreements reached to allocate the resources (financial and
workforce) as required by the regional model and set out in the
report.
 

iii) 
Endorse the approval already given in principle for Newcastle City
Council to support a North East Regional bid to become a Wave 2 RCC
national pathfinder, retrospectively endorsing submission of the
bid to DfE on 22 May 2026.
 

iv) 
Authorise the Director of Children’s Services in conjunction
with relevant lead member to take all necessary steps to implement
the recommendations in line with national policy.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve Newcastle City Council's participation in the expansion of the Regional Fostering Hub to improve support for foster carers and increase sufficiency of family-based care for children in the council's care.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The report will seek
approval of the notice of intention to commence Forth Yards
Masterplan Supplementary Plan under section 68 of the Town and
Country Planning (Local Planning) (England) Regulations 2026 and
delegate approval of public consultation on the draft Plan.
content:
The report will seek
approval of the notice of intention to commence Forth Yards
Masterplan Supplementary Plan under section 68 of the Town and
Country Planning (Local Planning) (England) Regulations 2026 and
delegate approval of public consultation on the draft Plan.

Cabinet agreed to:
 

i) 
Acknowledge the growing public and investor interest in the Forth
Yards area and significant opportunity for comprehensive
regeneration.

 

ii) 
Endorse the principle of preparing a Supplementary Plan which will
provide a planning policy framework for the Forth Yards area.
 

iii) 
Approve Notice of intention to commence the Forth Yards
Supplementary Plan preparation to cover the subject matters and
area to the timescale as set out in Appendix 1 of the report.
 

iv) 
Delegate authority to Assistant Director Planning, in consultation
with the Portfolio holder, to take all necessary steps to progress
the development of the Forth Yards Supplementary Plan including
preparation of a draft Forth Yards Supplementary Plan and carrying
out consultation on this (such consultation is proposed to take
place in Autumn 2026). Following this, the submission draft
Supplementary Plan will be presented to Cabinet for approval prior
to submission to Government for independent examination in
2027.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to prepare a Supplementary Plan for the Forth Yards area to facilitate comprehensive regeneration.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to refuse the
application
 
The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Licensing
Policy
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Guidance issued by the Secretary of
State
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
Mr Wilson explained to Committee that this
application and the basis upon which it is being made is almost
identical in nature to the meeting that Committee had considered
for his Client already earlier in the morning.
 
He confirmed again that Mr Gakhar already
holds a premises licence for premises at Dean Street and Grainger
Street in Newcastle and that it is desire to trade in a similar
operating style to those premises.  Mr
Wilson did state in relation to this application that Mr Gakhar
wishes to amend the hours to 10:00 until 22:00 hours
daily.  He is also willing to offer two
further conditions in the event that Committee are minded to grant
the application.  Firstly, a condition
that alcohol will only be sold if goods to the value of £5.00
are purchased and secondly a dynamic pricing condition would be
agreed as suggested in the representation from a local
business.
 
 
He accepts that the premises lie within the
cumulative impact area and special stress area and that special
policy 2 of the Council’s statement of licensing policy
applies.  He also accepted that the
burden is on the applicant to demonstrate that there are
exceptional circumstances and that if granted the application will
not add to the negative cumulative impact on one or more of the
licensing objectives. 
 
In seeking to discharge the burden Mr Wilson
stated that Committee should have regard to the fact that Mr Gakhar
is an experienced operator who currently holds a number of premises
licences.  These premises, if granted a
licence, will operate under a tight set of tailored conditions
which have been added to today at the hearing. The alcohol will not
be on display but will be kept in a separate locked storeroom which
should address concerns regarding visibility and/or potential for
theft.  Mr Wilson referred Members to
the proposed conditions which also include items such as training
and CCTV.  The premises will operate as
a convenience store and will not be alcohol led.
 
Mr Wilson confirmed when asked that the
applicant had not engaged with either the local councillor or the
local businesses about their representations.
 
He also confirmed when questioned by Mr Bryce
that there will be a minimum of two members of staff present both
of whom will be comfortable reporting people to the police in the
event that there is disorder.
 
 
Mr Bryce on behalf of the Licensing Authority
explained the basis of the Council’s statement of licensing
policy.  He confirmed that the CIA and
SSA had been established after consultation with multiple bodies
and consideration of data provided by many of those bodies.
Although Mr Bryce had no concerns about Mr Gakhar as an operator,
he did have concerns about the location of the premises, namely the
fact that they are opposite NX, one of the larger
nighttime  venues in the City, and the
effectiveness of the proposed conditions.  He stressed that the policy created a rebuttable
presumption of refusal in this case.
 
On behalf of Northumbria Police Sgt Cottis
stated that if granted the application the availability of alcohol
in the City would increase as would the potential for crime and
disorder and anti social behaviour. The conditions proposed do not
alleviate the concerns of Northumbria Police.  During the course of the hearing Mr Wilson
did ask if it would assist the Police should the applicant agree to
preclude the sale of alcohol whilst events are held at the NX venue
but Sgt Cottiss replied that her position would not change.
 
On behalf of Public Health Mr Cave stated that
data sets regarding public health are regularly updated and the
most recent data for the City Centre shows that an increase of
availability in alcohol causes increased issues relating to public
health and safety.  In
particular,  data shows an increase in
anti social behaviour, incidents of alcohol flagged crime and
admissions to hospital for alcohol and violence related
matters.
 
 
Committee considered all of the evidence
before it.  They read the written
representations of those who were not able to attend and gave
appropriate weight thereto.
 
They noted that the Council’s statement
of licensing policy clearly provided a rebuttable presumption of
refusal to grant new applications for off licences in the locality
in which these premises are situated. 
They acknowledged that each application is to be treated on its
merits and they noted the good character and lack of issues of the
applicant and his other premises. 
However they were of the view that this should be the norm rather
than justification of exceptionality. 
The Committee could see no reason to justify departing from policy
and concluded that the applicant had not demonstrated
exceptionality during the submission of the application or that the
application if granted would not add to the negative cumulative
impact on one or more of the licensing objectives,
namely  crime and disorder, public
nuisance and public safety.
 
 
Right of Appeal
 
There is a right of appeal against this
decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.
topline: The Committee has decided to refuse the application for a new off licence in a cumulative impact area and special stress area in Newcastle.

Gakhar already holds a premises licence for the ground floor of 62

convenience store.  Since opening in
September 2024 there have been very few crimes recorded in the
vicinity and no evidence that they relate to Mr Gakhar or his
operation of the shop and none relating to alcohol harm. Mr Wilson
explained that the purpose of the new application is to increase
the hours for the sale of alcohol from the premises which currently
has authorisation between the hours of 12 midday to 20:00.
 
He accepts that the premises lie within the
cumulative impact area and special stress area and that special
policy 2 of the Council’s statement of licensing policy
applies.  He also accepted that the
burden is on the applicant to demonstrate that there are
exceptional circumstances and that if granted the application will
not add to the negative cumulative impact on one or more of the
licensing objectives. 
 
In seeking to discharge the burden Mr Wilson
stated that Committee should have regard to the fact that Mr Gakhar
is an experienced operator who currently holds a premises licence
for these particular premises.  The
premises operate under a tight set of tailored conditions and with
this new application there are further restrictive conditions. The
alcohol will not be on display but will be kept in a separate
locked storeroom which should address concerns regarding visibility
and/or potential for theft. Mr Wilson referred Members to the
proposed conditions which also include items such as training and
CCTV.
 
When questioned as to why Mr Gakhar is seeking
an increase in hours, Mr Wilson replied that it is to be consistent
with other licensed premises operated by the applicant but also for
commercial reasons.
 
He also confirmed when questioned by Mr Bryce
that there will be a minimum of two members of staff present both
of whom will be comfortable reporting people to the police in the
event that there is disorder.
 
Mr Wilson confirmed that in the event that
this application is granted Mr Gakhar will surrender the existing
licence.  It is not his intention to
have two premises licences for the premises.
 
Mr Bryce on behalf of the Licensing Authority
explained the basis of the Council’s statement of licensing
policy. He confirmed that the CIA and SSA had been established
after consultation with multiple bodies and consideration of data
provided by many of those bodies. Although Mr Bryce had no concerns
about Mr Gakhar as an operator, he did have concerns about the
location of the premises and the effectiveness of the proposed
conditions. He stressed that the policy created a rebuttable
presumption of refusal in this case.
 
On behalf of Northumbria Police Sgt Cottis
stated that if granted the application would permit an extra 4
hours per day for the sale of alcohol into the City
Centre.  The availability of alcohol in
the City would increase as would the potential for crime and
disorder and anti social behaviour. The conditions proposed are not
as robust as those on the current licence.  Sgt Cottis appreciated the desire of the applicant
to emulate the operating style of Mr Gakhar’s other premises
on Dean Street but insisted that Dean Street is a very different
environment to Grainger Street which is very close to Clayton
Street.
 
Committee considered all of the evidence
before it. They noted that the Council’s statement of
licensing policy clearly provided a rebuttable presumption of
refusal to grant new applications for off licences in the locality
in which these premises are situated. 
They acknowledged that each application is to be treated on its
merits and they noted the good character and lack of issues of the
applicant and his other premises. However they were of the view
that this should be the norm rather than justification of
exceptionality. The Committee could see no reason to justify
departing from policy and concluded that the applicant had not
demonstrated exceptionality or that the application if granted
would not add to the negative cumulative impact on one or more of
the licensing objectives.
 
Right of Appeal

decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to grant the
application, as amended orally at the hearing by the Applicant.
This is subject to an amended schedule of conditions as agreed with
the Licensing Manager (attached to this decision notice).
 
The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Licensing
Policy especially paragraphs 4.7, 5.1, 6.1, 6.2, 6.3 and 7.
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Guidance issued by the Secretary of State
in particular paragraphs 1.16, 1.17, 1.18, 1.19, 2.1, 2.2, 2.3,
2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 2.20, 2.21, 2.22, 2.23, 2.24, 2.25,
2.26, 2.27, 2.28, 2.31, 2.32 and 9.12.
 
SUMMARY OF
EVIDENCE
 
Committee heard representations from Richard
Arnot, solicitor for the Applicant who outlined the nature of the
proposed operation, explaining that the premises would function
primarily as a pub restaurant. He confirmed that the Applicant was
well respected and experienced in local hospitality who had
successfully run several local bars and restaurants. The premises
would be known as Riverside Tavern also known as River God. The
intention would be for seating rather than vertical drinking.
 
Mr Arnot explained that he had engaged in
discussion prior to the application, together with site visits,
resulting in an agreed schedule of conditions with both Northumbria
Police and Environmental Health. The Licensing Authority agreed an
amended schedule of conditions shortly prior to the hearing.
 
He acknowledged concerns raised by both
Councillor Byrne and the local resident. The venue had previously
been a bar/nightclub which had had noise complaints raised. He
stated that the intention with the new venue was to have planned
music, but as a post meal entertainment and singer akin to 1950
Vegas style. A Noise Management Plan would also be drafted in
conjunction with Environmental Health
 
Mr Arnot also emphasised that the intention of
Mr Knox was to sympathetically protect, restore and renovate the
building to its former glory.
 
As regards the representation from local
resident, Mr Newton, constructive conversations had been had
between him and Mr Knox, who acknowledged the past problems at the
venue when a nightclub. Mr Knox was of the
opinion that he had allayed Mr Newton’s concerns.
 
As regards Planning, that representation
was considered to be informative to the
committee rather than an objection as it stated that planning
permission would be required.
As regards the representation from Councillor
Byrne, Mr Knox stated that he would have been happy to engage with
her had she reached out. He also commented that the premises is
already licensed, that this was not an additional premises.
 
Jonathan Bryce of the Licensing Authority
attended to offer rationale as to Licensing Authority agreement and
achieved compromise and addressed the committee and confirmed that
he has withdrawn representations based on agreed conditions that
proactively address the licensing objectives and are justified,
proportionate and enforceable. Councillor Williams asked what
assurances he could give about the Noise Management Plan, to which
Mr Bryce replied that the conditions were pre-emptive and he was liaising with the Applicant.
There would be continued noise surveillance and monitoring and
enforcement if necessary. The restoration would also enhance the
acoustic.
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
Committee carefully considered all written and
oral submissions presented in relation to the application. It took
particular account of the amended agreed
conditions as detailed within the agenda papers.
Committee noted the amended conditions which
the Applicant had agreed following engagement with the responsible
authorities. They were satisfied that the imposition of these
conditions meant there would be no additional negative impact on
the licensing objectives.
 
Conditions
 
As per the operating schedule attached to this
notice, with the amendments noted above.
 
Right of Appeal
 
There is a right of appeal against this
decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.
 
Licensing Authority
Proposed Conditions
 
1. The premises will operate as a
pub/restaurant with ancillary entertainment.
 
2. There will be no change to this operating
style without proper written notice to the Licensing Authority,
which shall include details of the operating style proposed. The
Licensing Authority shall advise within 21 days whether a formal
application for full or minor variation or a new licence is
required, and the licence holder shall comply with the
direction.
 
3. The Premises Licence Holder shall ensure
that all relevant members of staff receive training in their
responsibilities under the Licensing Act 2003. Staff training to
include Safeguarding and vulnerability training. Such training
shall be documented, and records made available upon request from
the Police or an authorised officer of the Licensing Authority.
This will include refresher training which shall be conducted at
regular intervals not exceeding 12 months.
 
Amended Conditions
which include those agreed with Northumbria Police and Revised by
the Licensing Authority
 
1. The Premises Licence Holder shall
ensure that at all times when the
Premises are open for any licensable activity there are sufficient,
competent staff on duty at the premises for the purposes of
fulfilling the terms and conditions of this licence and promoting
the licensing objectives.
 
2. The Premises Licence Holder shall conduct a
risk assessment for the general operation of the premises and any
individual bespoke events. The risk assessment shall be documented
and available for inspection by the Licensing Authority and the
Police on request. Such an assessment shall take into account levels of staffing and whether SIA
door staff should be deployed at any particular
times or for specific events
 
3. The maximum number of persons permitted on
the premises shall not exceed a figure prescribed by the risk
assessment undertaken by the Premises Licence Holder in compliance
with fire safety requirements.
 
4. The Designated Premises Supervisor, or
other member of management, shall ensure that there are effective
procedures in operation to ensure that the capacity figure
prescribed by the fire risk assessment is not exceeded.
 
5. The number and layout of the tables and
seating in the premises shall remain generally as depicted on the
deposited plan and shall not change without the consent of the
Licensing Authority.
 
6. Waiter/waitress service shall be available at all times the external areas are in
use.
 
7. The Premises Licence Holder shall not
knowingly permit the removal of alcohol in open containers beyond
the boundaries of the licensed area.
 
8. A CCTV system shall be designed, installed
and maintained in proper working order, to the satisfaction of the
Licensing Authority and the Police. Such a system shall:
 
(a) 
be operated by properly trained staff
 
(b) 
be in operation at all times that the
premises are being used for a licensable activity
 
(c) 
ensure coverage of all entrances and exits to the premises
internally and externally
(d) 
ensure coverage of such other areas as may be required by the
Licensing Authority and the Police.
 
(e) 
provide continuous recording facilities for each camera to a good
standard of quality. Such recordings shall be retained in an easily
downloadable format for a period of 28 days and shall be made
available to the Licensing Authority or Police on request
 
(f) 
whilst the premises are open a member of staff shall be available
at the premises who can retrieve CCTV footage and provide it to the
Police in an easily downloadable format within a reasonable
time.
 
9. An incident and refusals record shall be
maintained at the premises which shall record all relevant
incidents and refusals and shall be made available to the Licensing
Authority or the Police on request. The following shall be
recorded:
 
(a) 
the seizure of drugs or other illegal items
 
(b) 
all crime reported to the management at the premises or by the
management to the Police
 
(c) 
all ejections of patrons
 
(d) 
any faults in the CCTV system
 
10.No glassware or glass bottles shall be
deposited in an external skip or other receptacle between the hours
of 2200 and 0800 and any such skip or receptacle shall not be
removed from the premises between those hours.
 
11.There shall be maintained at the premises a
throw line/throw ring and staff shall be trained in the use of this
equipment.
 
12.The Premises Licence Holder shall operate a
Challenge 25 policy whereby any patron appearing to be under the
age thereof shall be required to provide suitable identification
before alcohol is served to them.
 
13.Acceptable forms of identification for the
purpose of Challenge 25 shall include a passport, driver's licence,
any recognised lD incorporating the
PASS logo, Military lD or any other
form of lD from time to time approved
by the Secretary of State.
 
14.All relevant staff shall be trained in
their responsibilities under the Licensing Act 2003.
 
15. No relevant member of staff shall be
permitted to serve alcohol until they have successfully completed
their training.
 
16. Refresher training shall be given at least
annually.
 
17.Training records shall be kept for each
relevant individual member of staff and such records shall be
provided to the Police or an authorised Officer of the Licensing
Authority on request.
 
18.The Premises Licence Holder shall maintain
a Noise Management Plan for the internal and external use of the
premises. The NMP shall be drafted with reference to Environmental
Health and the Licensing Authority and shall be made available upon
request to any Responsible Authority. The NMP shall include
standard operating procedures dealing with the management of the
external area.
 
19.Any temporary structures located at the
external area adjacent to the river shall be removed within 24
hours of any request made by the Environment Agency if such a
request is to facilitate the installation of temporary flood
barriers.
 
20.The Premises Licence Holder shall maintain
a refusal register which shall record all occasions when patrons
have been refused service of alcohol. This record shall include
details of the time and dated of the refusal, a description of the
patron, the reasons for refusal and which member of staff refused
service. This record shall be made available to the Police or the
Licensing Authority on request.
 
21.Staff training shall include an awareness
of 'proxy sales 'and staff shall refuse sale to anyone suspected of
intending to pass alcohol to anyone underage. Details of such
refusals shall be recorded in the refusals register.
 
22.A dispersal policy shall be implemented and
adhered to which shall encourage to leave the premises quietly.
This policy shall be made available for inspection by officers of
the Licensing Authority and Northumbria Police at any time the
premises is open for business.
 
23.An outside management policy shall be
adopted in relation to the supervision and management of all
outside areas. This policy shall be made available for inspection
by officers of the Licensing Authority and Northumbria Police at
any time the premises is open for business.
topline: The Licensing Committee has decided to grant a pub/restaurant application with amended conditions to address noise concerns and ensure compliance with licensing objectives.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to grant the
application subject to conditions.
 
 
The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Licensing
Policy
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Guidance issued by the Secretary of
State
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
 
Mr Williams started his presentation by
thanking the Responsible Authorities for conducting thorough,
independent reviews of their positions which had resulted in the
withdrawal of their representations.
 
He referred Members to September 2025 when the
Applicant had been before Committee with 2 similar applications to
provide LNR until the terminal hour of 05:00.  At that time there had been opposition to the
applications from Northumbria Police and the Licensing Authority
and in relation to one of the applications, Public
Health.  Committee on that occasion had
granted both applications and both premises have been operating
since without any particular issues specifically during the
licensable hours.  With regard to this
application,  Mr Williams explained that
since the first week in February of this year the premises have
been open and operating between the hours of 7am until 8pm and 8am
until 5pm on Sunday without issue. 
 
Mr Williams drew the attention of Committee to
the fact that the only outstanding representation was that of
Councillor Byrne who unfortunately was unable to attend
Committee.  He addressed both the
original representation and the supplemental statement provided in
relation thereto by Councillor Byrne. 
He submitted that the suggestion of 
Councillor Byrne that the application and conditions offered were
designed to respond to issues rather than prevent problems was
incorrect and cited matters such as CCTV which is proactive by
nature, provision of door staff which disincentivises crime and the
training of door staff with regard to conflicts as all being
evidence of the proactive approach of the Applicant.
 
The Committee accepted that the Applicant is a
reputable and well established operator both locally and
nationally.  They appreciated the
application and the conditions proposed by the
Applicant.  They were also aware that in
theory the applicant could operate 24 hours without a Licence so
long as they only served cold food and beverages between the
licensable hours of 23:00 and 05:00, however Committee felt that
regulation of a premises operating with enforceable conditions
would assist in ensuring that the licensing objectives are
upheld.
 
Committee noted and attributed appropriate
weight to the written submissions of Councillor Byrne but felt that
the conditions proposed were measures that would uphold the
licensing objectives. 
However, they also noted the lack of representation from
Environmental Health and the withdrawal of the representations from
the Responsible Authorities who had had concerns initially and on
balance they found that to grant the application would not
undermine the licensing objectives.
 
 
Conditions
 
As set out in the Committee papers.
 
 
 
Right of Appeal
 
There is a right of appeal against this
decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to grant
application.
 
The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Gambling
Policy
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Gambling Commission Guidance
 
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
Committee were advised that
this application related to a unit on Clayton Street that already
holds a Premises Licence.  The Licensing
Authority have received 2 applications in relation to that unit as
the applicant is seeking to separate the premises.  The matters before the Committee relate to a new
application for a Premises Licence Betting (other) in respect of
part of the existing premises and there a separate application for
variation of the existing premises licence for the unit to ensure
compliance in the event that the current application is
granted.
 
For the Applicant
 
Mr Wormald KC presented the application on
behalf of Luxury Leisure.  He referred
Members to the key submissions document contained within the
Committee papers.  He also referred to
the revised plan that had been submitted, various witness
statements, an independent report of Joanne Craig and an updated
LARA.
 
Mr Wormald explained to Committee the linked
nature of the 2 applications submitted by the
Applicant.  The application for a new
premises licence for Betting results from the separation of the
current unit at 54 – 60 Clayton Street into 2
parts.  The result will be a smaller AGC
premises and a modest area to be used as a Betting
premises.  The premises will have
separate entrances and the only access between them will be for
staff via an internal door with a glazed vision panel, provided
solely for health and safety purposes. 
Planning permission has been sought and approved for the
applications.
 
The Betting premises will operate without
gaming machines, there will be over the counter betting and SSBTs
only.  There will be clear lines of
sight between the entrance and the SSBTs.
 
Mr Wormald confirmed to Committee that a
compromise had been reached with the Licensing Authority during the
period leading to the Committee hearing resulting in the withdrawal
of the representation by Mr Bryce on behalf of the Licensing
Authority.  There are no other
outstanding representations other than that from a trade
competitor, Betfred. As part of his submission Mr Wormald
referenced the fact that the most recent communication from the
objector Betfred was dated 23 January 2026.  The end of the consultation period for the
application was 4 November 2025 and therefore in his submission
Committee should disregard the correspondence received after that
date from Betfred.
 
Mr Wormald submitted to the Committee that
there is a presumption in law that the Licensing Authority should
aim to permit gambling which presumption can only be displaced by
evidence, not speculation.  In his view
the submissions of Betfred are rhetorical rather than being
evidential.
 
When questioned by Mr Owens of behalf of
Betfred, Mr Wormald confirmed that at present the Applicant company
is not trading any of its premises in the manner currently applied
for, however he did clarify that a similar application had been
granted in Chesterfield very recently and will be opening soon.
 
For the Interested Party
 
Mr Owen started his submissions addressing the
comment regarding the “late” correspondence referenced
by Mr Wormald.  He explained that the
document dated 23 January 2026 was clarifying the position and
maintaining of representation of Betfred further to the revised
plans provided by the Applicant on 18 November 2025 but sent to
Betfred on 14 January 2026 and revised LARA provided on 19 January
2026 and sent to Betfred on 20 January 2026.  He stated clearly that the document of 23 January
ought to be considered by Members.
 
Mr Owens continued by stating that he had 8
points he wished Committee to consider in refusing to grant this
application.  The points he would
reference would show that the application was not consistent with 2
of the 3 licensing objectives.
 
Firstly his Client has issues regarding
inter-connectivity between the premises and the proximity between
the AGC and the Betting premises as initially also commented upon
by Mr Bryce.
 
Secondly, he wished for Members to have close
scrutiny to the “uniqueness” of the
application.  This will be the first
time that an application such as this has been determined by a
Committee.
 
Thirdly, the revised plan shows access between
the premises which Mr Owen submitted to be contrary to Guidance and
the Mandatory Conditions.
 
Fourthly, there is no precedent for a trading
style such as this currently operating in England. Newcastle, in
granting the application would essentially be a “guinea
pig”.
 
Fifthly, Betfred have a genuine concern for
the staff moving between premises and the fact that the two
premises will operate very differently is a cause for concern.
 
Sixthly, also regarding the interplay between
the premises there is concern for customer interactions.
 
Point seven, the size of the premises may be a
disincentive for staff to get involved should there be any issues
of crime and disorder or anti social behaviour.  The location of the premises is recognised as a
crime hotspot and betting shops do attract crime and anti social
behaviour.
 
Finally,  in his
words not the strongest of his points, Mr Owens stated that in
granting the application Committee may be opening the floodgates
which could lead to an over proliferation of premises.
 
REASONS FOR THE
DECISION
 
Committee considered as a preliminary matter
the submissions made by both parties regarding the acceptance of
the document from Betfred dated 23 January 2026.  They concluded that there would be no prejudice to
the Applicant in Committee considering the document.  They noted that the timeline from the end of the
consultation period had included revised plans, LARA and subsequent
withdrawal of the representation by the Licensing Authority in
light of those revised documents.  It
was clear that there had been a period of ongoing correspondence
resulting in significant changes to the application and Betfred
were entitled to respond thereto as indeed had the Licensing
Authority.
 
Committee noted the presumption of grant and
were persuaded further by the evidence of Joanne Craig that,
amongst other things, the policies and procedures proposed together
with the Local Risk Assessment would ensure that legislation
Guidance and Mandatory conditions would be complied with.
 
Committee noted that the Applicant is an
established professional operator with a good reputation who had
worked constructively with the Licensing Authority to achieve
compromise.  They noted that there were
no other representations from Responsible Bodies.
 
Committee were not persuaded by the
submissions of the Interested Party. 
They were aware that they must treat each application on its merits
and could not take into consideration matters such as proliferation
or the opening of floodgates.
 
In light of the fact that there were no
representations against the application to vary the AGC unit that
application was also granted.
 
RIGHT OF APPEAL
 
There is a right of appeal against this
decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.
topline: The Committee has approved a new premises licence for Betting in a unit on Clayton Street, despite objections from Betfred and concerns about the unique nature of the application.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to grant the
application subject to conditions agreed
 
 
The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Licensing
Policy
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Guidance issued by the Secretary of
State
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
Ms Nickerson explained to Committee that she
had recently purchased the premises which had previously operated
for many years as a coffee shop/café.  She still wants to primarily operate as a
café and for the benefit of the community but to also be
able to add the offer of alcohol.  She
stated that conditions have been agreed with the Responsible
Authorities and Ms Nickerson confirmed that she fully intended
sticking to those agreed conditions. 
Committee were referred to the relevant papers within the agenda
papers.
 
Ms Wallis on behalf of Environmental Health
explained that she is comfortable with the proposal so long as the
conditions are complied with. She accepted the terminal hour as
being reasonable and had noted that the premises had been
appropriately insulated with regard to noise during the
refurbishment thereof.  The premises
have 16 seats inside and 16 seats outside. All patrons will be
seated. The use of the external area which is privately owned will
be weather dependant.  It was confirmed
that there will be no seating to the rear of the
property.  Ms Wallis confirmed that
there had been no issues experienced when the business had
previously operated.
 
Mr Yeend described to Committee the location
of his home to the premises, namely next door approximately 1 meter
away.  He is fearful of noise nuisance
and odour from the premises and believes that the addition of
alcohol to the business will exacerbate problems.
 
Mr Oliver stated that the rear garden and
bedroom of his home abut onto the premises.  He believed that the offer of alcohol would
increase the attendance at the premises and is of the view that
intoxicated people would cause nuisance issues.
 
Mr and Mrs Thompson were concerned about
dispersal of patrons in the evening and it was clarified that it is
expected for dispersal to be staggered.
 
All of the residents who had expressed
objection verbally at the hearing mentioned concerns about traffic,
parking, issues with the unadopted highway and the potential for
decrease in house values, but it was explained that the Committee
could only take into consideration matters that impacted and
undermined the 4 licensing objectives.
 
Committee also had regard to the written
representations of those against and those in support of the
application and attached appropriate weight thereto.  Committee were grateful to the residents for
attending the virtual hearing and considered carefully their
submissions, however Committee were persuaded by the Statutory
Guidance that each Responsible Authority is an expert in their
respective field.  They acknowledged
that Northumbria Police and the Licensing Authority were not
objecting to the application due to their being satisfied with the
conditions that had been agreed with the applicant.  Committee found the evidence of Ms Wallis on
behalf of Environmental Health to be persuasive and were satisfied
that the operation of the business 
would not cause nuisance.
 
Accordingly, 
Committee concluded that to grant the application, subject to the
conditions agreed would not undermine the licensing objectives.
 
 
 
Right of Appeal
 
 
There is a right of appeal against this
decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.
topline: The Committee has decided to grant an application for a premises to operate as a cafe and offer alcohol, despite concerns from local residents about noise and nuisance issues.

decision_maker: Cabinet Member for Resources and Performance - Councillor Barry Phillipson
purpose:
The Crisis and
Resilience Fund (CRF) is a new government programme that replaces
the Household Support Fund and will run initially for three years
from April 2026. Its purpose is to bring together crisis support
and longer-term financial resilience activity through four strands:
Crisis Payments, Housing Payments, Resilience Services and
Community Coordination, with a strong emphasis on cash-first,
person-centred and needs-based support and clear referral pathways
to reduce repeat crisis. Newcastle City Council has been allocated
£5.9m for year one. While the overall direction of the Fund
is clear, detailed national criteria and delivery expectations have
been issued late in the planning cycle, limiting the time available
to design a fully developed local scheme ahead of go-live.
 
This report will seek
approval to implement interim arrangements for an initial six-month
period, ensuring continuity of support for residents while allowing
sufficient time to co-design a robust, high-quality and sustainable
three-year model that is well-governed and aligned with both local
need and national guidance.
content:
The Crisis and
Resilience Fund (CRF) is a new government programme that replaces
the Household Support Fund and will run initially for three years
from April 2026. Its purpose is to bring together crisis support
and longer-term financial resilience activity through four strands:
Crisis Payments, Housing Payments, Resilience Services and
Community Coordination, with a strong emphasis on cash-first,
person-centred and needs-based support and clear referral pathways
to reduce repeat crisis. Newcastle City Council has been allocated
£5.9m for year one. While the overall direction of the Fund
is clear, detailed national criteria and delivery expectations have
been issued late in the planning cycle, limiting the time available
to design a fully developed local scheme ahead of go-live.
 
This report will seek
approval to implement interim arrangements for an initial six-month
period, ensuring continuity of support for residents while allowing
sufficient time to co-design a robust, high-quality and sustainable
three-year model that is well-governed and aligned with both local
need and national guidance.

Use an initial
proportion of the Crisis and Resilience Funding to:
 

- 
Implement a crisis payment application process, allowing residents
in need to apply and receive a payment for support. It is proposed
an initial allocation of £0.1m from the fund to distribute to
those who meet the criteria. This would be administered by the
Senior Assessment Team within Revenues and Benefits.

- 
Use £2.1m of the funding for food vouchers for children in
receipt of free school meals during the school holidays for May
half term and summer 2026. This mirrors the provision that has been
given from the HSF since its inception in 2021 and the CRF for
Easter 2026.

- 
Rebrand Discretionary Housing Payments as CRF Housing Payments but
maintain the approach as delivered for DHP, using £0.7m
(including Housing Payment administration costs) from the fund as
directed by Government.

- 
Utilise up to 6% of the annual CRF grant for reasonable
administration purposes, in accordance with the scheme plus the
specified administration costs for Housing Payment element.
topline: The Cabinet Member for Resources and Performance has decided to implement interim arrangements for the Crisis and Resilience Fund to provide support for residents in Newcastle City Council.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to grant the
application in part and as follows;
 
The hours be extended as requested on Friday
and Saturday, the Sundays preceding Bank holidays and Christmas Eve
only.
 
The Conditions agreed be added to the Licence
with the following conditions also to be added;
 

1) 
SIA door staff be on duty on a Friday and Saturday evening and the
responsibilities thereof to be incorporated into the Management
plan to be agreed with Environmental Health.

2) 
The front door to the premises to be self
closing and to kept closed save for access and egress

3) 
There to be no admission of new customers to the premises after
23;30 hours..
 
The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Licensing
Policy
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Guidance issued by the Secretary of
State
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
Ms Smith explained to Committee that the
applicant and his brother, Andrew, have been in the hospitality
trade for a number of years. They have built an excellent
reputation and established a number of successful venues.
 
They seek to provide investment in local
communities and are also residents of Gosforth, the suburb in which
these premises are located.
 
Ms Smith stated that the premises had
previously held a licence which was transferred and varied in
November 2025.  The applicant has
invested £250,000.00 into the premises and it now  employs 18 staff, is open all day and is an asset
to the High Street.  It attracts a
diverse range of clientele, has 5star reviews on tripadvisor and is very popular.  The applicant is currently in the process of
opening a second venue in Ponteland.
 
Since taking over the premises the Applicant
has traded later hours using the TEN process and has done so
without issue.  Dialogue with
Northumbria Police and Environmental Health has been positive with
the Police agreeing to withdraw their representation following an
amendment to the requested days sought and the addition of
conditions.  It has also been agreed
that a management plan will be submitted for the approval of
Environmental Health.
 
The premises offer a strong food offering and
Members noted the comment from Northumbria Police that during a
visit by Officers at 10pm many people were eating and the kitchen
was still preparing food. 
 
Whilst the premises employ a DJ on Fridays and
Saturdays there is generally low key music.
 
The applicant has resolved issues with the
residents to the rear of the premises in Hawthorn Court by ensuring
adequate waste arrangements are now in place and the physiotherapy
business above is also comfortable with the application.
 
The applicant has engaged proactively with
both Mr Newton and Ms Francis who live above the neighbouring
premises with their young daughter. Acousticians have been employed
to agree sound levels, a noise limiter has been ordered and will be
set in due course. 
 
It was accepted that the applicant cannot be
held responsible for anything other than issues arising from the
use of his premises and as such it was agreed that customers who
wished to smoke would be guided away from the frontage of the
premises occupied by Mr Newton and Ms Francis.  It was also agreed that a bin would be installed
for smokers.
 
Committee accepted the evidence of Mr Newton
and Ms Francis that they very much appreciated the co-operation
shown by the applicant however they were still concerned about the
potential for noise and disturbance. 
They stated that people congregate after leaving the premises,
often in the  bus stop outside of the
premises waiting for taxis or just generally chatting.  They stated that the location of their
daughter’s bedroom means that her sleep is regularly
disturbed due to noise emanating from the premises.
 
After considering all of the evidence,
Committee were of the view that to grant the application to vary
the hours sought but not the request for the extension on a
Thursday evening, being an evening before school and work days,
would not undermine the licensing objectives.  Committee noted the conditions offered by the
applicant and the agreement with them by the responsible bodies but
were minded to impose further conditions having heard the
submissions of Ms Smith, on the basis that to do so would be
appropriate and proportionate to promote the licensing objectives,
specifically public nuisance.
topline: The Committee has decided to grant an application to extend hours for a premises in Gosforth, despite concerns raised by local residents about noise and disturbance.

content:
Planning permission
for application reference 2025/0784/01/DET be refused for
the following reasons:
 
 
i. 
The proposed introduction of a 59 space
basement car park as part of this development in an allocated
District Centre would attract additional vehicles to the site and
would undermine the prioritisation of the use of sustainable
transport modes to reach the site which is
located in a highly sustainable location. As such, the
proposed development fails to accord with paragraph 115 of the
National Planning Policy Framework, Policy CS13 of the Core
Strategy and Urban Core Plan and Policy DM11 of the Development and
Allocations Plan.
 
 
ii. 
The application does not include details of noise attenuation
measures for the proposed gym and ventilation system for the
basement car park. As such, the application does not demonstrate
how the amenities of residents of existing dwellings adjacent to
the site would be protected from unacceptable levels of noise
pollution and that the impact of any such noise pollution could be
mitigated to avoid it giving rise to significant adverse impacts
upon health and quality of life. As such, the proposed development
fails to accord with paragraphs 187 and 198 of the National
Planning Policy Framework, Policy CS14 of the Core Strategy and
Urban Core Plan and Policy DM24 of the Development and Allocations
Plan.
 
 iii. 
The application is not accompanied by a full engineering appraisal
or intrusive investigations sufficient to demonstrate that the high
stability risks to the development posed by shallow coalmine
workings as identified in the application documentation could be
satisfactorily mitigated. As such, the proposed development fails
to accord with paragraphs 196 and 197 of the National Planning
Policy Framework, Policy CS14 of the Core Strategy and Urban Core
Plan and Policy DM24 of the Development and Allocations Plan.
topline: The council has decided to refuse planning permission for a development due to concerns about sustainability, noise pollution, and safety risks.

decision_maker: Assistant Director Education - Paul Shadforth
purpose:
In order to meet
statutory duties under the School Admissions Code 2021, the local
authority (LA) is required to formally determine school admissions
arrangements for community schools every year, even where there has
been no change to the arrangements. The LA is the admission
authority for these schools.
All local authorities are required by the School Admissions
(Co-ordination of Admissions Arrangements) (England) Regulations
2012 to have a scheme in place each year for coordinating admission
arrangements for all maintained schools and academies (except
special schools and nursery schools) within their area. The scheme
has to comply with the provisions of the School Admissions Code
2021.
Co-ordination schemes are intended to simplify the admissions
process whilst reducing the likelihood of any child being left
without a school place. Co-ordination establishes a mechanism that
ensures as far as is reasonably practicable, that every parent of a
child living in a local authority (LA) who has applied to a
state-funded school is sent a single offer of a school place by
their LA.
The deadline to agree the proposed admissions arrangements for the
academic year 2027/28 is 28 February 2026.

decision_maker: Chief Finance Officer/ Section 151 Officer - Mark Nicholson
purpose:
The Crisis and Resilience Fund (CRF) is a UK
Government scheme from the Department for Work and Pensions (DWP).
It will commence 1 April 2026 and run until 31 March 2029. It
replaces both the Household Support Fund (HSF) and Discretionary
Housing Payments (DHPs).

Its purpose is to create a long term, sustainable system of local
support that provides immediate crisis assistance while
strengthening the financial resilience of low-income households
over time.

Provisional funding for Newcastle in year 1 is £5,926,670,
this is an increase of £115k from 2025/26 HSF and DHP funding
combined.

This report proposes the use of £245k of the funding to
provide Free School Meal vouchers for those who are eligible for
Easter 2026.

The remaining funding will be subject to further Delegated
Decisions.
content:
Use an initial £245k of the Crisis and
Resilience Fundingfor food vouchers for children in receipt of free
school meals during the school holidays for Easter
2026.
topline: The Chief Finance Officer has decided to use Crisis and Resilience Funding to provide food vouchers for children in receipt of free school meals during the school holidays for Easter 2026.

content:
The decision of the Committee is to grant the

The Committee in reaching its decision has
taken into account:
 
· 
The evidence before it both written and oral
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Council’s Statement of Licensing
Policy
 
· 
The relevant parts of the Guidance issued by the Secretary of
State
 
Committee’s reasoning and findings
are:
 
Mr Whur advised Committee that the application
to vary the licence had arisen following a compliance audit of the
premises by the Licensing Authority. The premises have operated as
Mojo since 2023 and the operator has invested £1
million.  They operate in other cities
with later hours to those in Newcastle. 
The operator is responsible and has had no issues since
opening.  The premises provide a premium
drinks and music venue.  He submitted
that the conditions that are the subject of the application are
outdated and redundant.
 
Committee were advised of the difficulties
currently faced by the hospitality trade and Mr Whur explained that
he had held constructive discussions with all parties who had
submitted representations.  He confirmed
that the outcome of those discussions had resulted in the
Responsible Authorities all withdrawing their
representations.  He expressed
disappointment that he had been unable to persuade Councillor Byrne
regarding her concerns.
 
Committee read the original and supplemental
representations of Councillor Byrne and attached the appropriate
weight thereto.
 
Committee were satisfied that to grant the
application would not undermine the licensing objectives.

content:
Planning permission for application reference 2025/1277/01/DET
was refused for the following reasons:
 

1. 
The property is situated within the Green Belt. The
construction of the new dwelling (annex building), extensions to
the original dwelling and garage block, and material change of use
of woodland and paddock to private garden by reason of their size,
siting, and scale, represents disproportionate additions over and
above the size of the original building resulting in substantial
harm to the openness of the Green Belt. The development and change
of use that has occurred results in a significant loss of openness
and encroachment into the countryside, contrary to the fundamental
aims and purposes of Green Belt policy as set out in National
Policy Framework and policy CS19 of the Core Strategy and Urban
Core Plan.

 

2. 
The development appears excessive, is visually
intrusive, and out of keeping with both the host property and the
wider landscape. The development does not represent a high standard
of design. As such, the application is contrary to the National
Planning Policy Framework, Policies CS4 and CS15 of the Core
Strategy and Urban Core Plan as well as Policy DM20 of the
Development and Allocations Plan.

 

3. 
The development has resulted in the unauthorised
loss of priority habitat and direct harm to a designated Site of
Local Conservation Interest (SLCI), Woolsington Estate and Adjacent
Woodlands, Woolsington TPO 08/1995. It has also led to the loss of
nesting habitat for protected and priority species, with no
adequate mitigation or compensation provided. The submitted
Biodiversity Net Gain assessment is inaccurate and fails to
demonstrate a measurable net gain. As such, the application is
contrary to Policy CS18 of the Core Strategy and Urban Core Plan
and Policies DM28 and DM29 of the Newcastle Development Allocations
Plan.
topline: The council has decided to refuse planning permission for a development in the Green Belt area, citing harm to the environment and conservation areas.

content:
DETAILS OF
APPLICATION
 
 
Details of the Application and copies of the
Representations and supporting evidence are attached to the Agenda
papers.
 
Committee’s
reasoning and findings are:
 
This is a hearing of a review application
dated 5th January 2026 for a review of the premises
licence for The County, 1529 Walker Road, Newcastle-upon-Tyne, NE6
3LB. The premises licence holder is Trust Inns Limited.  The review is brought under the provisions of S167
Licensing Act 2003 following a Closure Order made by South Tyneside
Magistrates Court on application of Northumbria Police under the
provisions of S80 of the ASBCP 2014. 
The effect of the Order was to close the premises on 5th
January 2026 for a period of one month.
 
At the hearing Trust Inns Limited sought the
disposal of the review by the removal of the DPS and the
modification of the conditions of the premises licence.
 
Committee were advised that a dialogue had
been entered into by Trust Inns Limited with the Licensing
Authority and Northumbria Police which had resulted in a Schedule
of Conditions being agreed between Trust Inns Limited and
Northumbria Police.  The Licensing
Authority were still in disagreement regarding the wording of a
number of those conditions.
 
Trust Inns Limited did not challenge or
contest the evidence of Northumbria Police or the Licensing
Authority during the hearing.  It was
noted that the DPS has been removed from position and that it is a
requirement that an application for the appointment of a
replacement DPS must be made to the Licensing Authority and that
Northumbria Police will be in a position to consider the
application.
 
Committee took into consideration the concerns
of the Licensing Authority regarding the proposed wording of
Condition 9 and the temporary nature of the requirement for Door
Supervisors.  However, Committee were
persuaded that along with a new DPS and a change in management it
would be appropriate to retain that requirement on a temporary
basis only. 
 
Committee accepted the suggestion by the
Licensing Authority that the wording in Conditions 1,7,10 and 11 be
changed to replace the word “Licensee” to
“Operator”.
 
DECISION
 
The decision of the Committee is as
follows:
 
To modify the conditions on the Licence which
they find to be a step that is appropriate for the promotion of the
Licensing Objectives.
 
To accept and replace the conditions on the
Licence with the Schedule of Conditions proposed by the Licensing
Authority/Trust Inns Limited and Northumbria Police save for the
amended wording referenced above in Conditions 1,7, 10 and 11.
 
 
Right of Appeal
 
There is a right of appeal against this
decision to Newcastle Magistrates Court.  An appeal must be commenced within 21 days
beginning with the day on which you receive written notification of
the decision.
